_comment: The retired browser transmit gate and three other implementations (two React settings modals
and the Python setup wizard) disagreed on which callsigns were valid, so the wizard showed
'Valid ITU Callsign' for callsigns the gate refused at slot start, and 'Invalid' for ones it
permitted. The three disagreements the audit measured are the first three 'divergence' cases.
Asserted by the retired TypeScript and Python implementations until they were removed
(2026-10-06 cleanup, last present at acfce5e). Kept because it was produced independently of
the Rust code; it must not be edited.
extra_rule: The base prefix (the part before any trailing '/suffix') must contain a letter.
_limits: This is a STRUCTURAL check, not an allocation lookup: it rejects an empty box, a name
typed into the callsign field and obvious typos, which is what the transmit gate needs.
It cannot tell whether a well-formed callsign was actually issued to the operator, and
well-formed strings that are not real callsigns (e.g. '111A') pass. Do not add cases here
that assert otherwise without changing the gate itself - and changing the gate is a
